newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Russia beating US for Japan aluminium market.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Russia beating US for Japan aluminium market.

text.p: Russian aluminium makers are gaining market share in Japan as the expense of United States producers, Greg Turnidge, managing director of Australian aluminium company Aluvic said on Thursday.

The loss of U.S market share is primarily due to the reduction of U.S. exports as consumers of the metal built up their inventories ahead of a global cost-cutting deal in 1993 and 1994, Turnidge told the Australian Bureau of Agricutural and Resource Economics.
"During this time, Russia had developed their Siberian railways, which opened up the Asian markets, where traditionally they transported their metal only to western Europe and China," Turnidge said.
Russian exports should continue to grow as smelters in Siberia seek to minimise transportation costs to reach final markets for their metal, Turnidge said.
"The Japanese are buying Russian metal at the widest discounts of any major market in the world," Turnidge said. "The cheap rates from Vavino and Nahadka (ports) are the reason."

Rusian AO-grade aluminium is fetching a discount of between US$40 and $45 a tonne under the prevailing spot London Metal Exchange price, while higher-grade A5 was priced at a premium of up to $15, Turnidge said.
A6-grade aluminium was prices at US$15-$18 a tonne over the LME, he added.
